item: BACKLOG spcc-sensor-curve section-4 test, arm A-prime (the doc's unrun counterfactual: a bare name WITHOUT the spcc_list preload, no save); GO #2a
instrument: Siril 1.4.4 flatpak siril-cli through scripts/lib/siril_run.py (-d sessions/july31); hand .ssf; no product written
ssf_verbatim:
requires 1.4.0
setcompress 0
setext fit
set32bits
load ../../web/results/july31/stack_set-01_full_wcs
spcc -catalog=localgaia "-oscsensor=Nikon D750" "-oscfilter=No filter" "-whiteref=Average Spiral Galaxy"
close
use_line_verbatim: log: SPCC will use OSC sensor "Nikon D750" and filter "No filter"
prediction: source-predicted (docs/spcc-sensor-curve-z6iii.md section 1.2): the names resolve BEFORE the database loads, so the run silently uses index 0 of the OSC lists (Canon EOS 1D Mark III x Antila RGB_ultra_ii) while echoing "Nikon D750"; K then differs from B-double-prime's 0.697/0.945

verdict.reading: MEASURED: a bare name without the preload is NOT honoured — the log echoes "Nikon D750" (line 52) before the metadata loads (53), and K 1.000/0.681/0.911 with R/G fit 0.531138+0.607751x sigma 0.247630 (the worst sigma of the three arms) differs from both the index-0 control (0.687/0.927) and the preloaded D750 run (0.697/0.945); WHICH model was in force is the source's prediction (index 0 of the OSC lists), not read from the log — the echo names the requested string, not the resolved entry

premises_not_tested: the identity of the model in force (Canon EOS 1D Mark III x Antila RGB_ultra_ii) — predicted from the 1.4.4 source's byte-sorted lists, not printed by Siril; a probe naming that pair explicitly WITH the preload would test it (K should equal this arm's 0.681/0.911)
that a bare name without preload is deterministic across runs (one run)
